A Preliminary Study on Seating Selection Tendencies and Preferencences Among UIN Walisongo Medical Students in the Classroom

Studi Pendahuluan mengenai tendensi dan Preferensi Mahasiswa Kedokteran dalam memilih posisi duduk di Ruang Kelas di UIN Walisongo

Fahmi Achmad Darojat

Faculty of Medicine, Walisongo State Islamic University

Manuscript preview

This manuscript is displayed for review. Peer-review and acceptance status have not been supplied; it has not been assigned to a published issue.

Abstract

Seating positions in the classroom are not coincidental or random phenomena, but are thought to reflect each student's personal factors, both in terms of personality and the environment that influences them. In high- intensity academic environments such as medical education, understanding these tendencies can provide deep insights into the learning engagement, motivation, and dynamics of each student, both personally and in groups. However, specific research highlighting the medical student population is still limited.

Therefore, this preliminary study aims to map the tendency of medical students to choose their seating position (front, middle, back, right, left) and explore the reasons behind these choices. In addition, the phenomenon of male and female students separating will also be examined.

This study uses an exploratory mixed-methods design. Quantitative data is obtained through data on the relationship between age, academic grades, and seating position from front to back. Qualitative data is collected through a questionnaire administered to 27 respondents from medical students at Walisongo State Islamic University to explore their motivations, perceptions, and factors influencing their choices.The results show that the biggest factors in seat selection are the presence of close friends and the smoothness of learning.

Keywords

Seat position · Medical students · Tendency
